Prohibition in case of officers of Supreme Courts, against accepting gifts

[THE SUPREME COURTS' OFFICERS TRADING ACT, 1848]
[THE SUPREME COURTS' OFFICERS TRADING ACT, 1848]
(Short title given by the Short Titles Act,
1897 (14 of 1897).)
ACT No. XV of 1848
[17th June, 1848]
An Act to forbid trading by the Officers of the Supreme Courts
1. Prohibition in case of officers of Supreme Courts, against accepting
gifts. No officer of any of the Courts of Judicature established by Royal
Charter within the territories subject to the government of the East India
Company, or any Court established for the relief of insolvent debtors within
the said territories, shall directly or indirectly by himself, or by any other
person or persons on his behalf, accept from any person or persons any gift or
reward for any act or behaviour in his office, other than his legal salary and
fees and profits of office, or hold any office in any bank or public company,
except as hereinafter excepted or carry on or be con cerned in any dealings as
a banker or trader or as agent, factor or broker either for his own advantage
or for the advantage of any other person or persons, except such dealings as it
may be part of the duty of any such officer by virtue of his office to carry
on.

Exemption of officers who are also advocates, etc

[THE SUPREME COURTS' OFFICERS TRADING ACT, 1848]
[THE SUPREME COURTS' OFFICERS TRADING ACT, 1848]
(Short title given by the Short Titles Act,
1897 (14 of 1897).)
ACT No. XV of 1848
[17th June, 1848]
An Act to forbid trading by the Officers of the Supreme Courts
2. Exemption of officers who are also advocates, etc. This Act
shall not be construed to forbid any officer of any of the said Courts, who is
also a practising advocate, attorney, solicitor or proctor in any of the said
Courts, from taking the usual fees and emoluments of advocates, attorneys, solicitors
or proctors, nor to apply to any advocate, attorney, solicitor, proctor,
sheriff, assignee, receiver or committee, so far as he is held to be in that
capacity merely for some purposes and officer of any of the said Courts.

Holding unpaid office in society

[THE SUPREME COURTS' OFFICERS TRADING ACT, 1848]
[THE SUPREME COURTS' OFFICERS TRADING ACT, 1848]
(Short title given by the Short Titles Act,
1897 (14 of 1897).)
ACT No. XV of 1848
[17th June, 1848]
An Act to forbid trading by the Officers of the Supreme Courts
3. Holding unpaid office in society. This Act shall not be
construed to forbid any officer of any of the said Courts from holding any
unpaid office in any so ciety for charitable purposes or for the advancement of
knowledge, or for the encouragement of science, art or manufactures.

Punishment for contravention of Act

[THE SUPREME COURTS' OFFICERS TRADING ACT, 1848]
[THE SUPREME COURTS' OFFICERS TRADING ACT, 1848]
(Short title given by the Short Titles Act,
1897 (14 of 1897).)
ACT No. XV of 1848
[17th June, 1848]
An Act to forbid trading by the Officers of the Supreme Courts
4. Punishment for contravention of Act. Every officer of any of the
said Courts who shall know ingly offend against this Act shall, on conviction
thereof, be liable to be punished by deprivation of his office, and also, by
the sen tence of the Court before which he shall be convicted, may be declared
incapable, and in that case shall become incapable, of being appointed to the
same or any other office of the same Court, or to serve (Subs. by A. O., 1961, Art. 2 (with effect
from the 23rd March, 1956), for "Her Majesty".)[Government] (The words "or the East India Company
" rep. by the Repealing Act, 1876 (12 of 1876).)* * * in the territories under the government of the East India
Company, or in such part of the said territories as shall be specified in the
sentence, or in the discretion of the Court may be otherwise punished by fine
or fine and imprisonment for his misdemeanour as to the Court shall seem fit,
regard being had to the nature of his offence.
